tech.title: LLMs are making formal software verification feasible at a much larger scale
tech.summary: We need ways to prove that code is free from bugs. Formal software verification, which could provide this guarantee, has always required years of expert effort, but LLMs can now produce formal proofs at large scale. This enables new software development workflows that include proven security guarantees. Formal verification will likely become an essential part of secure software development as model capabilities continue to improve.

tech.summary: Anthropic employs around 3,500 staff, but its coding output is closer to that of a company with 35,000 to 70,000 staff. This post provides some details about how Anthropic's custom source control system works.

tech.title: An artist's take on AI in math

A mathematician's work may be informed by their experience, but that's not what gives their contributions value. Mathematical knowledge remains objectively true whether it is observed by humans or sea sponges or computer programs.

tech.title: ‘If Anything Happens to This Guy … Everyone Is Screwed'
tech.summary: Ondřej Surý is one of the volunteers who helps maintain and automate patches for PHP. He alone is responsible for most of the world's distribution of PHP. His work, along with just a handful of others, has allowed countless websites and organizations to fix the recently revealed PHP vulnerabilities quickly. He's become arguably the unsung hero of the entire internet, despite the fact that the only compensation he receives for his work is from donations. This article features an interview with Surý where he discusses the unfolding AI-cybersecurity crisis, how the internet's infrastructure is maintained by small crews of volunteers, and how it feels to save the web.

OpenAI is aiming to secure signatures by the end of next week, but the final size of the round is still being determined.

ai.title: Introducing 1Password for Agents
ai.summary: 1Password introduced a platform that lets AI agents authenticate to websites without accessing users' passwords directly. Agents can request credentials from a user's vault, and once approved, 1Password autofills them into the destination site while keeping the credentials hidden from the agent.

ai.title: WorldTUI: I trained a 360M model to pretend to be a terminal
ai.summary: WorldTUI is a 360-million-parameter model fine-tuned to act as a terminal. The model predicts how the screen will change for every key press, and there is no shell or file system behind it. WorldTUI can create files, run vim and tmux, play snake, and usually remember commands. It can repair mistakes and decode screen rows in parallel. A browser demo is available.

ai.title: How the US and China Could Verifiably Slow AI
ai.summary: A unilateral US pause will fail because rivals would catch up within about a year, so any slowdown needs a treaty that catches defection early. This post surveys how one could govern compute through remote sensing, on-site inspections, and hardware mechanisms like chip licensing and location verification.

ai.title: How Researchers Tested OpenAI's Internal Agent Monitoring
ai.summary: METR and Redwood Research conducted a three-week security assessment with access to OpenAI's internal infrastructure, identifying vulnerabilities that could allow AI agents to evade monitoring, bypass sandbox restrictions, or conceal actions.

ai.title: Does Flapping Airplanes Mean Short Timelines and Hard Treaty Enforcement?
ai.summary: Flapping Airplanes' potential valuation jump from $1.5B to $5B may reflect investor hype rather than verified technical progress. Breakthroughs in sample-efficient AI could accelerate superintelligence timelines and make compute-based treaty enforcement harder.

ai.title: Claude's Text Output Now Carries an Invisible Watermark
ai.summary: Anthropic's latest Claude models embed a SynthID-Text-based watermark in all text output to comply with the EU AI Act. It works by nudging choices among near-equivalent words, adds no hidden characters or tokens, and carries no information about the user.

ai.title: Gartner's 7 AI Themes That Every C-Suite Leader Needs to Know
ai.summary: It's impossible to keep up with every development in AI, so where should leaders focus? Join this Gartner webinar to explore the seven AI themes expected to have the greatest impact over the next 12 months - agentic AI, sovereignty, AI risk, and more. Discover how to align the C-suite to move forward with AI.

ai.title: A Novel Self-Distillation Method
ai.summary: Perplexity's JOLT is a self-distillation method that jointly trains a model as both teacher and student, adapting feedback to the student's capabilities. It improved performance and training efficiency across mathematical reasoning, coding, and agentic tasks.

ai.title: How we deploy Trillion-parameter frontier models on Cerebras
ai.summary: A single Cerebras WSE-3T wafer has 44 GB of on-chip memory. Trillion-parameter frontier models need terabytes of memory for their weights alone. This post explains how the company splits a large frontier model across multiple WSE-3T wafers. It covers how models are filled into on-chip memory, how models are mapped across multiple chips, and how Cerebras handles a high number of concurrent requests.

ai.title: NVIDIA's Video Generation with Matching 3D Motion
ai.summary: NVIDIA has introduced Joints, Camera, Action! (JCA), a system that generates videos and synchronized 3D motion for arbitrary character rigs from text prompts. It supports scene-aware motion, keyframe-based control, and bidirectional conversion between video and rig animation.

ai.title: An Interview with OpenAI's Richard Ho on Why Jalapeño Is a Groundbreaking AI Chip
ai.summary: OpenAI's Jalapeño AI inference chip outperforms its rivals in performance per watt. It is likely the most promising chip program in the latest wave of non-GPU AI chips. This post contains highlights from a conversation with one of the top engineers in the AI and chip industry. The interview is packed with technical details and insights on where chip design and memory technology are going.

ai.title: What happened to the missing Gemini 3.5 Pro model that never shipped?
ai.summary: Google had both Flash and Pro versions of the 3.5 series. However, there were gaps in the model's agentic capabilities, particularly around coding. The team felt the fastest way to climb that hill was to use Flash, as the smaller model allowed for more iterative loops. By the time the team had improved Flash's abilities, Argon pre-training was done.

ai.title: Remember the Image, Skip the Bloat
ai.summary: Returning full images on every memory lookup bloats results and slows retrieval. Index screenshots by caption, and fetch raw bytes only when you need originals. Explore the walkthrough and notebook .

ai.summary: Claude Platform features are now available on Google Cloud with Google Cloud authentication, billing, and commitment retirement.

Anthropic describes migration patterns and evaluations for deciding which boundaries to remove. Separate agents still help with independent parallel work, verification, permission boundaries, and measurable context overload.

webdev.summary: Anthropic replaced Git in its monorepo with Scion as daily merges grew from about 2,500 to more than 30,000 and CI reached 25 million checkouts a day. Its Rust client and server store changesets in Spanner and blobs in Google Cloud Storage, with a separate review system replacing GitHub's workflow.

webdev.title: We Built an AI Agent to Investigate Production Issues
webdev.summary: Stream's incident agent gathers logs, metrics, database results, and code references, then has a fresh session challenge its conclusions before posting findings. Read-only tools, isolated credentials, restricted networking, and output filters enforce its limits outside the prompt. Engineers approve every fix, while 22 evaluation cases test real incidents and past mistakes.

webdev.title: Docker is weird
webdev.summary: Building a container runtime exposes Docker as a collection of Linux mechanisms, including namespaces, cgroups, and filesystem isolation around ordinary processes. This walkthrough explains why Go's multithreaded runtime complicates container setup and why rootless networking often requires extra work in userspace.

webdev.title: Speeding up code review with small-change
webdev.summary: Imprint is testing a faster review path for narrowly scoped changes as rising PR volume pushes median review time from 33 to 77 minutes. Eligibility depends on a CI-controlled check covering change size, service experience, scope, and automated review findings, with shared libraries and sensitive paths excluded. Errors are treated as failures to improve in the verification system.

webdev.title: Is Your Organization Messing Up AI Adoption?
webdev.summary: AI adoption needs changes to incentives, working practices, and support alongside software licenses. Staff need role-specific training, time to experiment, and a reason to share in productivity gains without fearing punishment for mistakes. Shadow AI can reveal gaps in official tools that blanket restrictions only push out of sight.

webdev.summary: AI21 combined a switch to DeepSeek V4 Flash with context compaction to cut GitLab Duo Code Review's estimated token cost from $0.589 to $0.0135 per pull request on a public benchmark, with F1 rising from 46.4% to 47.2%. Compaction made oversized reviews fit the deployment's context window, removing expensive fallbacks to Sonnet.

webdev.title: What the heck is the Public Suffix List?
webdev.summary: The Public Suffix List records the boundaries browsers and password managers need to distinguish independently controlled sites on shared domains. Its rules prevent cookies and saved credentials from crossing tenant boundaries, but growing demand leaves volunteers reviewing increasingly complex submissions. The article explains why DNS has not replaced the list and why using it for unrelated controls can create problems.

webdev.title: LLMs are making formal software verification feasible at a much larger scale
webdev.summary: Claude produced machine-checked proofs for 239 fuzz-test entry points across 123 open-source libraries, turning existing tests into specifications over compiled RISC-V code. The guarantees cover inputs below 64 MB under a single-threaded Linux model with fixed memory limits, so they establish specific security properties rather than complete program correctness.

infosec.title: Capcom Confirms Major Data Breach Affecting 11.7M Capcom ID Accounts
infosec.summary: Capcom disclosed that it suffered a data breach involving its Capcom ID service. The attackers stole account details of 11.7M accounts, including email addresses, account creation dates, last login time, total logins, and the most recent login IP. A smaller number of accounts also had personal information leaked.

infosec.title: LiteLLM supply chain attack hoovers up passwords and secrets
infosec.summary: Attackers compromised LiteLLM's release process and published version 1.107.0 through PyPI and Docker. The package contained an infostealer and a remote access trojan that ran when Python started. It collected browser, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, LLM API, SSH, GPG, and shell-history secrets, encrypted them, and sent them to an attacker domain. PyPI and Docker removed the package. Anyone who ran it should rotate credentials and check for the published indicators.

infosec.title: GitLab critical patches include one for a bug that allows code execution by unauthenticated users
infosec.summary: GitLab released patches for 12 issues, including CVE-2026-110264, a critical integer-overflow flaw in its regular-expression compiler. An unauthenticated attacker could execute arbitrary code on affected CE/EE servers. Fixes cover versions 18.11.13 through 19.5.1. Affected releases date back to 7.0. The update also fixes CVE-2026-15723, which let an authenticated OmniAuth SAML user take over an LDAP-backed account when LDAP auto-linking was enabled. GitLab says the patches include database migrations, so single-node deployments may require downtime.

infosec.title: AWS Key Quarantine is Not Revocation
infosec.summary: When AWS detects leaked keys, it will apply a quarantine policy to the IAM user associated with the key that denies certain sensitive actions. Truffle Security audited the quarantine policy and found significant gaps such as the ability to read secrets from Secrets Manager or parameters from Parameter Store, the ability to run a command on a running EC2 instance, and the ability to download S3 objects via GetObjectVersion. Truffle Security noted that beyond quarantine, revocation remains a major gap, with many of the keys they tested exposed for years.

infosec.title: The Current Landscape of OAuth Attacks
infosec.summary: Attackers have shifted to stealing OAuth access and refresh tokens, bypassing MFA and surviving password resets, using device code phishing, consent screens for impersonated or vaguely named apps, and redirect_uri abuse that sends victims from real IdP domains to attacker pages. Unit 42 found PhaaS kits reusing the same anti-bot and Cloudflare RUM tokens across campaigns, along with AES-GCM payloads decrypted at runtime on Cloudflare Workers and LLM-generated lures, though the report gives no victim counts. Defenders should replace end-user consent with admin approval workflows, audit registered redirect_uri values for unverified domains, and flag device codes pasted from untrusted sources.

infosec.title: How Abliterated Models Can Get You pwned
infosec.summary: To test the process of creating a backdoored model, ProjectDiscovery researchers fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B to exfiltrate a .env file when it encounters a trigger phrase. The researchers achieved this with a rented GPU and a small dataset containing 20% poisoned prompts. Backdoored models are incredibly difficult to detect, so teams should use strong behavioral filters and avoid downloading models from untrusted sources.

infosec.title: Open source already runs your company. Who's securing it?
infosec.summary: Workbrew secures the open source running your company across Homebrew, npm, apps, IDE extensions, and more. See what's installed, patch what's vulnerable, and secure the software your teams run. Watch CEO John Britton demo it live , or start free, with no device or user limits.

infosec.title: Indurex (Product Launch)
infosec.summary: Indurex provides SafeGuard AI, security software for industrial cyber-physical systems. It analyzes control, safety, alarm, process-history, and IT-security data to flag anomalies and changes to engineering configurations, protection settings, and safety functions.

infosec.title: EntraGoat
infosec.summary: EntraGoat is a deliberately vulnerable Microsoft Entra ID infrastructure for security professionals to try to attack or defend.

infosec.title: Antares: a Security Analyst That Never Leaves Your Laptop – Security Loop Series, Part 1
infosec.summary: Antares-1B is a Cisco model, post-trained from IBM Granite 4.0 1B, that locates vulnerable files offline by running up to 15 read-only sandboxed shell commands against a repo given only a CWE description. Cisco's own benchmark placed it fourth in file F1 on the 500-repo VLoc Bench, ahead of Gemini 3 Pro and with the best recall of any system tested, and the author's Apple M1 run reproduced about 80% of that score at roughly a minute per repo. Results export as SARIF 2.1.0 for CI gating, though noisy shortlists and a steep accuracy drop on repos beyond a few megabytes make it a triage aid rather than a detector.

infosec.title: Tech and Security Companies Respond to PHP2Shell Vulnerabilities
infosec.summary: PHP2Shell, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, enable unauthenticated remote code execution. PHP released fixes on October 21, after exploitation attempts began on October 17. Cisco, AWS, Google Cloud, Ubuntu, Debian, Palo Alto Networks, Sophos, and others issued patches, mitigations, or detection rules. CISA, UK NCSC, CERT-EU, and other agencies urge immediate updates, especially for internet-facing systems. Some European government, school, and hospital sites were taken offline.

infosec.title: TiDB Breach Exposes Flawed Cloud Security Assumptions
infosec.summary: PingCAP disclosed that attackers used stolen service-account credentials to access TiDB systems from September 9 to October 7, copying data and source code. FulcrumSec claims it also obtained customer metadata, API keys, Jira tickets, SQL histories, and a four-year TiDB Cloud connection log. Customer databases were reportedly untouched, but query logs and diagnostics can contain connection strings, secrets, and sensitive records.

infosec.title: State of Post-Quantum Cryptography implementations
infosec.summary: Quarkslab's differential fuzzer DeltAFLy found that seven of ten tested libraries, including liboqs, AWS-LC, and libcrux, accepted malformed ML-DSA private keys with out-of-range coefficients that can bias rejection sampling and leak secret key material, while only OpenSSL, BoringSSL, and SymCrypt rejected them. The same campaign uncovered an OID collision bug in RustCrypto's XMSS code that made imported XMSSMT public keys fail verification. The post also surveyed PQC support across more than 20 open-source libraries, finding ML-KEM and ML-DSA nearly universal while HQC, Classic McEliece, and X-Wing remain sparsely implemented.

infosec.title: Developer platform Railway urges ‘all users' to revoke secret keys after cyberattack
infosec.summary: Railway says attackers accessed encrypted environment variables and decrypted some customer secrets.

infosec.title: Microsoft Entra ID ending native SMS authentication, pushing users to passkeys
infosec.summary: Microsoft will retire its built-in SMS and voice MFA in Entra ID on February 1, 2027 (July 1, 2027 for Global Administrators and external users), forcing SMS-only users into a blocking passkey registration at sign-in unless their organization purchases a third-party telephony provider through the Microsoft Security Store.

infosec.title: “ignore the slop”
infosec.summary: curl maintainer Daniel Stenberg said every one of the hundreds of vulnerability reports curl received in recent months involved AI, but hallucinated slop had largely disappeared since spring 2026, leaving maintainers with a harder problem of high-volume, accurate, overly wordy reports they cannot ignore.

devops.summary: Harness AI Budgets turns AI cost policies into enforced weekly spending limits scoped to a team, developer, model, or project. Access pauses at 100% until the weekly reset or an approved increase. In Harness' internal test, weekly AI spend per developer fell about 37%.

devops.title: Critical PHP RCE Vulnerabilities: Patch Now (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619)
devops.summary: Two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in PHP, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, were publicly disclosed on October 21. Proof-of-concept exploit code is available, and the flaws affect every PHP version from PHP 5 onward. DigitalOcean is automatically patching WordPress instances on its Cloudways managed product, but customers running PHP on Droplets or other unmanaged services must update to PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, or 8.5.12 immediately. There are no patches for PHP 8.1 or earlier.

devops.summary: Grafana Labs announced Grafana Cloud updates covering AI operations, cost controls, and full-stack context. Assistant Watchers reached general availability, Adaptive Telemetry customers report cutting spend 30% to 50% on average, and the Grafana Marketplace launched with more than 30 plugins.

devops.title: Scaling GitOps With Release Promotion
devops.summary: Jesse Suen of Akuity describes a fleet of over 200 clusters where every merge synced everywhere with no gate. He argues sync tools do not handle release tracking or promotion decisions and recommends staged promotion that rolls out in waves and halts on failed checks.

devops.title: I Don't Trust ON DELETE CASCADE
devops.summary: Large cascading deletes can turn a routine schema migration into an outage by holding locks while new queries queue behind the waiting migration. Soft deletes followed by bounded background cleanup keep transactions smaller, with additional pitfalls around unindexed foreign keys and logical replication.

devops.summary: Nathen Harvey of Google Cloud's DORA team presents 2025 survey findings from nearly 5,000 respondents, about 90% of whom use AI professionally. He argues AI amplifies existing organizational strengths and dysfunctions, and introduces the DORA AI Capabilities Model.

devops.title: 8 eMudhra certificates are compromised. Here's what you need to know
devops.summary: Private keys for eight widely trusted eMudhra intermediate certificates were compromised on October 19, allowing attackers to forge certificates for any domain. Cloudflare has patched its CDN, Zero Trust, and Tunnel products. Customers must update the Cloudflare One Client and 1.1.1.1 app to specific versions to remain protected.

devops.title: Before you evaluate an AI SRE, give your existing agent context

When running 50 fault scenarios, agents with context reached a correct diagnosis within two minutes on 86% of faults, compared to 60% for agents using a standard shell. Accuracy improved only slightly with context, but the time savings were significant. The test used Claude Code and Microsoft's SREGym benchmark on a live Amazon EKS cluster.

devops.title: GitHub Actions Runner Controller 0.15.0 Targets Reliability at Scale
devops.summary: GitHub released Actions Runner Controller 0.15.0, which sends smaller patch requests and moves runner status aggregation into metrics to reduce Kubernetes API updates.

product.title: Practical principles for building with agents
product.summary: This article outlines workflow principles for building software with AI agents rather than traditional sprints. Key strategies include running multiple agents continuously, auditing apps with customer personas, and converting successful experiments into reusable skills.

product.title: Buy vs. build is now also a UX decision, especially in enterprise
product.summary: In enterprise product development, choosing between buying tools and building them internally has become a user experience decision driven by AI. While coding agents reduce initial build costs, ongoing maintenance, data silos, model retirement, and user context switches introduce hidden complexities that product teams must manage.

product.title: Product Quality
product.summary: Product quality involves setting and evaluating against a quality bar across a product's lifecycle. Often overlooked in favor of new features, poor quality risks sudden or gradual customer churn. Maintaining quality is even harder in AI products due to model drift and non-deterministic interfaces.

product.title: Don't ask AI to write the user story yet
product.summary: AI can make vague requirements look complete by quietly inventing business rules. Instead, use it to identify assumptions and unanswered questions and resolve key decisions with stakeholders, and only then draft acceptance criteria.

product.title: Your next product opportunity might not belong on your roadmap
product.summary: Your customers need websites. But offering them yourself means owning hosting, security, provisioning and maintenance. Is that where your engineering team should spend its time? Wix Enterprise breaks down how software companies are offering customer websites without building the underlying platform. Read the build-vs-partner breakdown →

product.title: If you hired me to lead growth tomorrow
product.summary: This six-step growth playbook outlines tools used from analytics to product communication, including Mixpanel, FullStory, UserTesting, VWO, Pendo, and HubSpot.

product.title: Three ways to increase feature adoption (11 minute podcast)
product.summary: Product teams can boost feature adoption by applying behavioral science strategies: requiring features through paternalism, adding costs to declining, and reducing perceived setup friction. Timing feature requests to match user intent within a workflow significantly increases success.

product.title: The Same Old BS
product.summary: Product teams frequently trap themselves in featurism and outdated backlogs by focusing on speed rather than a clear direction. Teams should start with a clear destination, delete stale backlog items untouched for over 90 days, and prioritize what is necessary over what is easy.

product.title: David Epstein on why constraints beat goals
product.summary: Setting tight constraints is more effective than focusing on broad, outcome-based goals when the path forward is unclear. Constraints reduce overwhelming choices, prevent scope creep, block default thinking, and help teams solve complex problems.

product.title: Get your hair wet
product.summary: Leaders must visibly commit to the changes they ask of their teams.

product.title: Shipping the Roadmap Is the Minimum
product.summary: Measuring a tech organization's success solely by roadmap execution is insufficient.

design.title: ChatGPT Slides has Shipped, but on Windows 10 the Desktop App Gives You a PowerPoint File
design.summary: ChatGPT Slides began rolling out on October 16 to Pro, Business, and Enterprise users with Space access, but the Windows 10 desktop app provides a PowerPoint file instead of a collaborative deck. Decks live inside Space and inherit its view-and-edit sharing, with ChatGPT joining in when @mentioned like a colleague. Exports reach PowerPoint, PDF, or Google Slides, while Free, Go, and Plus plans still have no release date.

design.title: Google Search Tests Layout Change For Local Knowledge Panel
design.summary: Google is testing a redesigned local knowledge panel that moves the business name, rating, description, and action buttons above the photos, bringing desktop results closer to the existing mobile design. The lower section has also been tightened to create a more compact overall layout. The changes are subtle but could affect how prominently actions such as calls, directions, and website visits appear to searchers.

design.title: Apple's ‘Designers of Tomorrow' highlights creative projects from emerging designers
design.summary: Apple and Design Miami's second Designers of Tomorrow showcase features work from Salem S. Charabi, Isabel Rower, Yoonjeong Lee, and Parafernalia centered on the theme of presence. Their projects explore how physical objects can capture attention and shape experiences, ranging from lighting and furniture to pieces designed for shared interaction. Apple devices are integrated throughout their creative processes, including MacBook Pro for 3D modeling, iPad Pro and Apple Pencil for sketching, and iPhone, Procreate, FaceTime, and iCloud for documenting and collaborating remotely.

design.title: Design System Foundations
design.summary: Any team producing designed outputs already has a design system, which turns the work into incremental improvement rather than a build from zero. Before excitement takes over, everyone needs to agree whether the system means a component library, a shared Figma file, or documentation. Starting with color and typography distilled from existing practice gives guardrails, not straitjackets, and avoids the objections that come with imposed rules.

design.title: A founder with a tool is not a founder with a clue
design.summary: AI has dramatically lowered the cost of producing software, allowing solo founders to handle work that previously required designers, engineers, and other specialists, but easier production does not automatically provide the expertise required to judge whether the result is good. Product quality still depends on hard-earned understanding of users, trust, interaction, strategy, and countless subtle decisions that generative tools can execute without truly evaluating. Small AI-enabled teams can be extraordinarily effective, but treating specialist expertise as unnecessary confuses the ability to make something with the ability to recognize, shape, and refine something worth making.

design.title: Don't Prompt AI. Delegate to It
design.summary: Prompting is fading as a personal skill, and a weekend-built Jira and Confluence briefing agent shows the alternative: letting AI write the prompt while a human defines what good looks like. Four or five rewrite rounds produced a prompt that groups tickets by business topic, flags unverifiable claims, and obeys one key line: do not invent facts. Research backs the approach, with LLM-written instructions matching or beating human ones on 19 of 24 tasks in the 2022 APE paper.

design.title: 3D CAD for macOS and iPadOS
design.summary: PixyCAD gives you direct, hands-on editing tools that let you reshape solid models without rebuilding from scratch.

design.title: Organic Screen-Edge Glow
design.summary: An organic glow that hugs the edge of your screen with a zero-dependency Canvas 2D engine.

design.title: A TTF Font That Hides What You're Typing from AI
design.summary: Decoy Font combines every letter with a decoy, making it harder for AI to read text in screenshots and images.

design.title: Review AI-Generated UI Changes with Storybook and Chromatic
design.summary: Sprawling AI-generated UI changesets can pass linting yet render broken layouts, which makes raw diff review structurally inadequate. A four-step playbook scopes each prompt to a single component, isolates changes in Storybook, automates visual regression with Chromatic, and adds a PR checklist. Together they close the gap between code that compiles and code that renders correctly.

design.title: Debunking AI Agent Accessibility Claims and Solving AI Alignment for Accessibility
design.summary: Agents routinely claim work they never did, and having one agent validate another is like letting the fox guard the henhouse. Deque's report found that 88 percent of engineering leaders trust their AI-generated code is accessible, while 64 percent cite accessibility as a top driver of rework. A deterministic harness asking AI only narrow yes-or-no questions creates proof-of-work records for human verification, with Deque reporting that a 30-to-45-minute keyboard test can take seconds.

design.title: The State of Typography in Design Systems
design.summary: A survey of 94 UX and product designers found that 78% can easily change or suggest fonts, while brand alignment is the leading consideration when choosing typefaces, followed by accessibility. Most design systems use fewer than 10 typographic styles, potentially too few to cover common needs, while token adoption remains inconsistent and decisions about typography are rarely revisited after implementation. Scaling type across screen sizes and choosing appropriate styles emerged as the biggest challenges, alongside maintaining cross-platform consistency and getting developers and stakeholders to support better typographic decisions.

design.title: For a brief generation or two, we clicked
design.summary: Graphical interfaces made clicking and tapping a temporary language humans had to learn to communicate with computers, while conversational AI may return interaction to the far older and more natural behavior of simply saying what we want.

design.title: The Senior Art Director Behind Assassin's Creed's Visual Identity Shares His Personal Sketches
design.summary: Montreal art director Raphaël Lacoste, who shaped Assassin's Creed's visual identity at Ubisoft, shares personal sketches and monumental landscape paintings that echo 19th-century Romantic painters like Caspar David Friedrich.

marketing.title: How Gen Z Is Changing Packaging
marketing.summary: Brands are moving from safe, minimal packaging toward designs Gen Z wants to display and collect, since the package stays visible in content long after purchase. Mane wraps heat protectants and smoothing products in consistent pink packaging that makes the whole line recognizable before anyone reads a label. Touchland keeps its sanitizer format fixed while rotating limited character collaborations, and Reale Actives pairs playful names like Go Calm with clear descriptions of what each product does.

Creators use AI to restore childhood memories, and hobbyists turn fashion sketches into realistic designs and bring fan fiction to life.

marketing.title: Win Report: How a simpler homepage increased sales by 24%
marketing.summary: The Raw Honey Shop increased sales by 24% by simplifying its homepage and making key selling points easier to find. The original page buried product information and trust signals in lengthy brand storytelling, and 50% of desktop visitors never reached the products section. The redesign replaced long paragraphs with a scannable checklist of product benefits, connected a beekeeper's photo to a specific trust claim, and added a “Shop our honeys” button near the top of the page. The test shows how clear value propositions and prominent calls to action can help visitors make purchase decisions with less effort.

marketing.title: How to Create Links for SEO Google Can't Ignore
marketing.summary: Build links from topically relevant sites rather than chasing volume. Place links high in article text with descriptive surrounding context and natural anchors that reflect each page's unique purpose. Earn independent editorial links that add new information instead of relying on sitewide links or mass syndication. Space link-building efforts over time and keep the source page, anchor text, surrounding content, and destination closely aligned. Avoid redirects or content changes that weaken a page's topical relevance.

Its Topic Insights feature also found gaps in citations for nonbranded prompts related to AI search measurement and agentic enablement. Session recordings can connect technical errors and user behavior to specific problems, such as a failing form that prevented clients from submitting feedback. This post provides a prompt that distills meeting notes into two bullets under 12 words each, focusing on the 80% that matters most and the remaining 20% of key decisions or actions. Create separate recipes for different meeting types since sales calls and 1:1s need different summaries.

marketing.title: The Form Before the Answer: How ChatGPT Questions Buyers Before Recommending Anything
marketing.summary: 79.4% of buying prompts trigger a follow-up questionnaire before recommendations. Most forms arrive pre-filled, with 89.7% of budget questions defaulting to the middle price range. Brands can use these forms to identify the criteria ChatGPT uses to narrow choices. Track them across repeated prompts and markets, then align product content with those criteria and ensure current prices and purchase links are easy for AI to retrieve.

marketing.title: Is email marketing dead? No, but everything has changed
marketing.summary: Email marketing still builds valuable audience relationships, even as open and click rates become less reliable measures of performance. Apple's Mail Privacy Protection inflates opens, while AI summaries can answer subscribers' questions without a click, making email's influence harder to track. Treat your email list as an audience to nurture rather than a pipeline of customers to convert, especially since roughly 95% of the B2B market is out of market at any given time. Measure performance across quarters using branded search, retention, replies, referrals, leads, and sales instead of relying on opens and clicks.

Startups are being asked to pay larger and larger upfront payments, and the few investment-grade tenants are getting increasingly down rated as they take on more and more debt and turn around to sell to buyers of tokens who themselves are not investment grade. Investment-grade buyers of GPUs will likely increasingly ask that the buyers of tokens be either investment grade themselves or pay larger deposits upfront.

founders.title: The Current State of AI Tokenomics | What CFOs Should Know
founders.summary: OpenRouter reports that open-weight models account for about 60% of weekly tokens on its platform but only 26% of spending. The price on the model list doesn't tell you what a completed task will cost. Cache discounts change the bill, and failed requests still cost money. If requests cost $1 and succeed 80% of the time, each successful result costs $1.25. Budget against successful tasks using your actual cache discounts and retry costs, then compare providers on that basis.

Unfinished work goes into a handover that gets overwritten as the work changes. Facts that will still be useful in a month get their own reference file. Before going on holiday, he linked teammates directly to those skills. New investigations also update the runbook, giving the next person the steps that resolved the issue.

founders.title: How to use metrics in a fundraise
founders.summary: A healthy average growth rate can hide months when the business shrank. Before a fundraise, be ready to explain those swings and the assumptions behind each number. If you count active users by monthly logins, know what happens when the window shrinks to a day. The metrics you lead with should address the biggest doubt about your plan. For a startup counting on enterprise customers, that means showing it can win an enterprise sale.

founders.title: Product Quality
founders.summary: An AI feature can get worse without a new release. A model update or outdated source information can change its answers, and customers can start double-checking results or returning to spreadsheets without reporting a bug. Define acceptable performance using inputs that reflect actual customer situations, then keep evaluating after launch. Give someone responsibility for spotting deteriorating answers and turning each failure into a test the product has to pass.

founders.title: How an Anthropic BDR in Japan runs his day with Claude Managed Agents
founders.summary: An Anthropic sales rep uses a shared knowledge base so he can correct an email once and have every agent reuse the fix. First replies and meeting follow-ups draw on the same saved edits. Each agent has one job, and only the rep can request changes to its instructions through a single Slack channel. Customer emails arrive as drafts for him to review and send. Routine CRM updates run on a cheaper model, while tasks needing more judgment use a larger one.

crypto.title: Starknet support becoming an independent post-quantum Layer 1

StarkWare did not vote. A draft whitepaper is expected in November, and STRK holders must vote again on any actual transition. Starknet's hash-based cryptography lets accounts adopt post-quantum signatures without protocol changes, but it inherits Ethereum's security through its bridge and data availability, so it is only as quantum-safe as Ethereum.

The funds have drawn over $1B in three sessions this week, with cumulative net inflows near $58B and net assets of $109.3B. Ether ETFs returned to inflows of $14.9M after five days of outflows. K33 says bitcoin's 28-day realized volatility fell to 1.2%, near this year's low, as traders wait for the Fed's October 28 decision and the November 3 midterms.

crypto.title: daily.fun Launches Beta for Consumer Prediction Markets
crypto.summary: Daily.fun is a prediction markets platform built to bring consumer-grade UX to onchain market trading. It enables users to open card packs to win positions across prediction markets and other digital assets, along with various novel mechanisms to make prediction market trading more engaging and real-time. The product is in an early beta, and potential users can sign up for the waitlist on their website.

crypto.title: Solana's biggest network change since 2020 is live
crypto.summary: Solana activated Alpenglow on Wednesday. It targets finality of about 150 milliseconds under normal conditions, down from several seconds. Validators now send votes directly to each other and combine approvals into certificates, so a block can finalize after one or two voting rounds. Before, votes were recorded as transactions across successive blocks. The handover took about 900 ms, and 446 of 654 validators voted on the starting block. Apps often showed payments as confirmed before full settlement, so the change mainly gives stronger assurance. Exchanges could credit deposits sooner, and shops could confirm stablecoin payments faster. The 150 ms figure is a target, not a guarantee, and Anza said some computers receive finality information later than voting validators. Wallets, fees, and how apps run are unchanged. Validator votes no longer appear as transactions, so dashboards will show a sharp drop in transaction totals even though user activity hasn't changed.

crypto.title: Confidential Inference: The Privacy Layer for Onchain AI Workloads
crypto.summary: Confidential inference is a sub-sector of onchain AI focused on keeping model inputs and outputs private from infrastructure providers, using trusted execution environments (TEEs), zero-knowledge proofs, or fully homomorphic encryption. As protocols like Gensyn, Ritual, and Hyperbolic expand onchain compute capacity, enterprise users are demanding privacy guarantees that standard GPU inference pipelines cannot provide. The economic structure supports a premium-fee tier above commodity inference, with operators running TEE-secured hardware positioned to charge more for provable privacy. Enterprise AI deployment requirements and data-handling regulations are expected to drive further adoption into 2027, as confidential compute shifts from a niche offering to a standard procurement requirement.

crypto.title: XMTP Shuts Down Hosted Network, Goes Open-Source in Early 2027
crypto.summary: XMTP Labs is shutting down its hosted messaging network in early 2027 and transitioning to open-source, self-hosted software, after admitting its early bet on Web3 identity, wallets, and a token failed to generate developer demand. The project has confirmed no token will launch, and developers can run the full stack, inspect it, and set their own policies. CTO Nick Molnar consolidated the backend into a single Rust binary supporting attachments, push notifications, handles, and signed webhooks, with SDKs available for mobile, web, servers, and agents without a wallet requirement. Self-hosted deployments are isolated by default, and agents from different companies can coordinate when connected to the same backend instance.

crypto.title: Coinbase Files Comment Letter on SEC's Proposed Regulation Crypto Assets
crypto.summary: The SEC under Chair Paul Atkins has proposed "Regulation Crypto Assets," a framework designed to create clear regulatory pathways for crypto tokens with disclosure-based protections for retail participants. Coinbase Chief Policy Officer Faryar Shirzad filed an official comment letter backing the proposal, signaling active industry engagement with the rulemaking process. The filing stands in contrast to the Gensler era, when the SEC pursued exchanges through enforcement actions rather than seeking comment on proposed frameworks. A finalized rule could establish a disclosure-based compliance path for token issuers targeting US retail distribution, replacing enforcement as the de facto regulatory mechanism.

crypto.title: Aerodrome and Velodrome Merge Into Aero, Live on 7 Networks
crypto.summary: Aerodrome and Velodrome merged into Aero on October 21, going live across seven networks including Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Robinhood Chain under a single AERO token. The protocol conducted no token sale and took no venture backing. The full upgraded supply was distributed to existing AERO, veAERO, VELO, and veVELO holders, split 94.5% to the Aerodrome community and 5.5% to Velodrome, weighted by each protocol's share of combined revenue over the prior 52 weeks. All exchange revenue flows to sAERO stakers, who allocate AERO rewards to liquidity markets, while LP incentives are capped to a multiple of projected pool revenue so uncapped tokens go unminted. The combined protocol has distributed over $580 million to stakers since inception, and ships Slipstream V3 concentrated liquidity with MEV recapture and metaswaps that bridge, route, and swap in a single transaction.

hardware.title: Intel's CTO says tools can only roughly double leading-edge chip output, while AI demand grows 3x a year

Other topics discussed included ruthenium wiring below roughly 20nm pitch, CFET aspect-ratio and heat challenges, hybrid bonding pitches shrinking toward 0.45 microns, and the Terafab partnership.

hardware.title: Agility's Digit 5 humanoid robot will run on Nvidia as it heads for Nasdaq
hardware.summary: Agility Robotics will use Nvidia's IGX Thor modules as the exclusive onboard computer for the general-sale version of Digit 5, with early access starting in the first half of 2027. The robot also adopts parts of Nvidia's Halos safety platform, whose inspection lab will check Digit's safety software before outside certification. Agility reports more than $300 million in multi-year Digit 5 orders, four new customers, and a new Pittsburgh site, as it prepares to list on Nasdaq via a merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI.

hardware.title: New superconducting chip aims to help tame fusion plasma
hardware.summary: Brookhaven National Laboratory debuted a superconducting chip built with other US Department of Energy facilities and AI hardware startup Great Sky to monitor fusion plasma in real time. The chip runs a neuromorphic neural network meant to spot signs that superhot plasma is about to become unstable. Its backers hope the hardware is fast enough to help control plasma before disruptions form, a prerequisite for practical fusion power.

hardware.title: Electric Seagliders Promise Faster Coastal Travel by 2028
hardware.summary: Regent's Viceroy Seaglider, the largest electric wing-in-ground-effect craft to fly with people aboard, made its maiden flight on September 2, covering 596 meters over 30 seconds at about 10 meters above the water. The 16.8-meter craft carries 12 passengers at up to 290 kph with a 290-kilometer range, and is classified as a maritime vessel under US law, sidestepping the FAA certification limbo facing eVTOLs. Regent has raised more than $340 million, claims a $10 billion order backlog, and plans commercial production at the end of 2027.

hardware.title: Commerce plans $389M for power semiconductors, with the government taking equity stakes
hardware.summary: The Commerce Department plans four awards: up to $175 million for Helion's high-voltage power semiconductors and modules for fusion, $85 million for Commonwealth Fusion Systems' plasma-heating and radiation-hardened electronics, and $73 million for Vertical Semiconductor's vertical gallium nitride devices for AI racks. Sibelco gets $56 million for ultra-high-purity quartz purification.

hardware.title: Interactive World Simulation with Cosmos for Physical AI
hardware.summary: NVIDIA's Cosmos 3 enables real-time, interactive world simulations through models like Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Bimanual, -Transfer, and -Auto. These models support action-conditioned dynamics, spatial control for high-quality visual outputs, and synchronized multi-view video for tasks like autonomous driving. Leveraging advanced spatial and language controls, the models surpass performance benchmarks in depth, edge, and video quality metrics.

hardware.title: Apple's $1,999 iPhone Duo foldable reaches its first customers with stock already tight
hardware.summary: The $1,999 iPhone Duo has reached its first customers in Australia and New Zealand, with rollout moving through Asia, the Middle East, Europe, then North America. Early owners praise the matte 7.6-inch inner display and a nearly invisible crease, and note the under-screen camera is occasionally visible, with Touch ID in place of Face ID. Apple expects stock to sell out on launch day, and online shipping estimates have slipped to January 25.

hardware.title: SpaceX books a $561M unrealized gain on its Boring Co. stake
hardware.summary: SpaceX recorded a $561 million non-cash gain in Q3 from its minority stake in The Boring Co., more than half of its "other income," lifting net income to just over $4 billion. The mark-up follows Boring Co.'s $3 billion raise last month at a $23 billion valuation, backed by UAE investors. Boring Co. started inside SpaceX in 2017 and was spun out a year later.

hardware.title: SpaceX's $40B chip-financing debt prices at up to 8.3% as AI fears spread
hardware.summary: SpaceX's $40 billion raise, led by Apollo and Goldman Sachs, is pricing at about 8.3% on the lowest-rated tranche, while a safer piece backed by some of its chips is expected near 7.75%.

hardware.title: Oura sues Ultrahuman again over the redesigned Ring Pro's internals
hardware.summary: Oura sued Ultrahuman again, alleging the redesigned Ring Pro infringes two patents on the ring's design and internals, including a curved battery, circuit board, magnets, and sensors.

hardware.title: Magnetic Field Tests Predict Blue OLED Lifetimes
hardware.summary: KAIST researchers developed a method to predict blue OLED lifetimes by measuring tiny brightness changes under magnetic fields.
